transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ari Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Kim (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Redwood CSM), Tom Reyes (Riverton CTO), Maya Singh (Riverton Head of Data), Devon Park (Riverton Security), Lena Ortiz (Riverton Product)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff to align stakeholders, review security and network constraints (VPC, KMS), pick sandbox region, and agree next steps for SSO and trial dataset. Confirmed interest in Dedicated vs Hosted evaluation; customer leans hosted first then Dedicated for production.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ari: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we're waiting on one person but wanted to kick us off. I'm Ari with Redwood on the growth team, and Leah our SE is here to walk through technicals. Jordan from CSM will run the onboarding tasks.
[00:18] Tom: Hi Ari, Tom here, sorry a minute late. We have Maya, Devon and Lena on. Excited to get started.
[00:24] Ari: Great. Quick agenda: intro, success criteria, security/network, sandbox and data, timelines, and next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:33] Maya: Yep that works. We're particularly focused on data residency and encryption, and how you handle PII in logs.
[00:40] Leah: Totally, we'll cover KMS, audit logs, and retention. A quick note up front — many customers start on hosted to iterate, then move to Dedicated or Private for stronger isolation. No hard push, just what tends to work.
[00:57] Devon: For us, SOC2 and SSO are must-haves before any production rollout. We also need the ability to bring our own KMS keys.
[01:06] Leah: Absolutely, BYOK is supported. We integrate with common KMS providers and can support customer-managed keys via our control plane in Private or via dedicated KMS in Dedicated. Sometimes the language in the security doc can be a little noisy, I'll share the exact snippets.
[01:25] Lena: Timeline wise we want a pilot within two weeks and a production decision in six weeks. Is that feasible?
[01:33] Ari: Two-week pilot is doable — we'll need a small sandbox, a couple dev seats, and some sample traffic. For production in six weeks we should start the security review immediately.
[01:44] Jordan: I'll open the onboarding workspace and invite the folks you mentioned, Lena and Maya. I'll also share the checklist and coordinate the pilot kickoff.
[01:51] Tom: On the pilot, we want to test chat and embeddings for search + triage. Cost is a consideration; what are the usual levers?
[02:00] Leah: Main levers are batching, KV cache (we sometimes say K-V cache in docs), and model quantization. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per workload. We'll show a couple examples in the tech deep-dive.
[02:12] Tom: Any immediate blockers for sandbox region? We prefer us-west-2.
[02:16] Leah: us-west-2 is available for hosted sandboxes; Dedicated sizing depends on quota. For the pilot we'll spin up a hosted sandbox there.
[02:25] Devon: About logs — we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and sensitive fields redaction. How does that work?
[02:31] Leah: You can route audit events to your syslog/Splunk or S3; we have row-level obfuscation options. A note: some of the auto-generated logs may include partial prompts unless you enable prompt stripping — we'll send the exact settings.
[02:50] [00:03:00] Maya: Regarding SSO, we use Okta. How long does SAML mapping usually take?
[02:56] Ari: ~1-2 days to configure and test if you have a dedicated admin. Leah will share the SAML metadata and example mappings.
[03:05] Leah: I'll also add a sample terraform snippet for the RBAC groups so you can auto-provision users.
[03:12] Tom: Good. For encryption in flight and at rest, any particular certs or ciphers we should be aware of?
[03:18] Leah: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit, and AES-256 for at-rest; when BYOK is used the keys stay in your KMS. There's occasionally confusion in the doc where it says HSM vs KMS — we'll clarify.
[03:33] Devon: We need to confirm whether model artifacts are stored outside our VPC in Hosted. If we go Dedicated, are artifacts kept in our tenancy?
[03:40] Leah: In Hosted, model artifacts are managed by Redwood; we provide encryption but not tenancy. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and options for customer-managed storage depending on the contract. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the only mode with artifacts inside your network.
[03:58] [00:05:00] Lena: OK, sounds good. For the pilot, do you recommend any particular model family? We want low latency for chat but also good quality for triage.
[04:08] Leah: A common pattern is start with a mid-size open model we verify in our catalog, use Redwood Optimize to get batching/quantization tips, then for production you can either move to a larger model or use a cheaper variant with caching for cost control. We'll propose a few candidates after we see your sample prompts.
[04:26] Tom: On the topic of costs, can you provide an estimated spend envelope for the pilot? Even ballpark.
[04:31] Ari: Yes — we'll provide a ballpark based on expected tokens per request and requests per minute. I'll put together a simple estimate once you share traffic patterns.
[04:39] Maya: We'll send a sample set of 500 requests/day and target p50 latency under 300ms.
[04:46] Leah: 300ms p50 is achievable on hosted for small models, but depends on sequence length and concurrency. We'll run a bench. There may be some transcription glitch in the performance doc where a number was typed incorrectly — we'll double-check.
[04:59] [00:10:00] Jordan: I'll draft a milestone plan: day 0-3 invite and SSO, day 3-7 sandbox and sample dataset load, day 7-14 pilot run and bench, day 14 review. Does that timeline map to your expectations?
[05:10] Tom: Yes. One more thing on compliance — we need a SOC2 attestation and a copy of your encryption key rotation policy.
[05:18] Ari: We have SOC 2 Type II; Leah will attach the cert and the key rotation summary. Devon if you want deeper legal text we'll route you to legal.
[05:28] Devon: Please send the DOCS to security@riverton.internal and make sure any sample config has no production keys.
[05:34] Leah: Noted. We'll scrub samples.
[05:40] [00:15:00] Maya: On data — we will anonymize PII but want to test redaction and also the opt-out flow. Can Redwood handle explicit deletion requests tied to a session id?
[05:50] Leah: Yes, we have deletion APIs and retention controls per route. There are some caveats with cache invalidation (prefix or KV cache), we'll provide the exact sequence to ensure deletion across caches.
[06:05] Tom: Are there limits for number of routes or custom models in sandbox?
[06:09] Leah: Sandboxes have modest quotas — we'll bump as needed for the pilot. If you decide to go Dedicated, quotas scale with the reserved capacity.
[06:20] [00:20:00] Lena: Who will be our main CSM contact?
[06:24] Jordan: That's me, Jordan. I'll be your primary and will do weekly check-ins during the pilot, then handoff to onboarding if you go into production.
[06:33] Tom: Great. On the network side, we might require a peered VPC for private deploy later. How does Redwood do peering?
[06:41] Leah: For Private we do VPC peering or transit gateway integrations depending on cloud. There's occasionally a misunderstanding in our docs between peering and private link — we'll clarify in the network checklist.
[06:55] [00:25:00] Ari: Quick recap and asks: Ari will send pricing and onboarding checklist; Leah will share SSO, KMS, and audit log docs; Jordan will open the workspace and invite users; Maya will share sample dataset and success criteria. Anyone want to add?
[07:11] Maya: Please include the sample prompt set and target evaluation metrics — we'll want to run an eval.
[07:16] Leah: We'll attach an eval template and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:23] Tom: Also, can we do a short perf run with our 500 requests/day profile next Tuesday?
[07:29] Ari: Yes, we'll schedule a perf bench — Leah and Jordan will coordinate a slot.
[07:34] Devon: One more security ask: proof that encryption keys are rotated and can be auditable.
[07:39] Ari: We'll include the key rotation summary and the SOC2 report.
[07:44] [00:30:00] Jordan: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run and the technical deep dive (model routing + quantization).
[07:51] Lena: Sounds good. Any known gotchas we should be aware of?
[07:55] Leah: Sometimes customers forget to strip PII in the sample dataset; also keep an eye on long prefix caching behavior if your prompts have sensitive patient IDs — we'll show how to configure prompt stripping. Also, latency targets can change with long sequence lengths.
[08:12] Tom: Ok noted. Thanks everyone, I'm comfortable with the plan.
[08:17] Ari: Great — we'll send notes and the artifacts we discussed. Jordan will be the point for scheduling. Thanks all.
[08:24] [00:40:00] End of recording.

Post-call notes:
- Files shared: onboarding checklist (link), SAML metadata (link), security pack (SOC2 PDF link), eval template (link) — links to be sent in follow-up email.
- Customer committed to pilot start next week; internal stakeholder list confirmed.
